messages:
marta_support: FYI customer ACME just ran a burst throughput test against their dedicated pool and we're seeing p95 jump from ~120ms -> 650ms during a 30s window. Also observed a few 502s. Customer says avg tokens per request ~450, peak ~2k.

sara_support: ack. can you paste a couple of request IDs and the exact wallclock time range? helps SRE pull logs.

marta_support: sure — sample request ids: req-0a12b3c4, req-0d34f5e6, req-0f56a7b8. Window: 2026-03-15T14:02:10Z -> 2026-03-15T14:02:45Z. They reported ~800 rps sustained for ~20s with bursts to 1100 rps.

eli_sre: thanks. couple quick asks so we can build a repro kit:
- full sample payloads (one short, one long)
- concurrency profile (clients, per-second schedule)
- average + max token counts (you said 450/2k)
- exact model and pinned version + quantization settings used by the customer
- whether they used prefix/KV caching or not

sara_support: I'll ask them for payloads and the client-side load script. also ask if they used caching.

jay_prodeng: for reproduce, best to provide a curl example + a small wrk/hey script so we can re-run locally. e.g.:
```bash
# replace $TOKEN and endpoint
curl -v -X POST "https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rwd-ggml-7b", "input":"<trimmed-prompt>", "max_tokens":200}'
```
and a minimal wrk wrapper:
```bash
wrk -t8 -c200 -d30s --latency 
  -s ./scripts/post.lua --  https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
(we use post.lua to POST the payload)

eli_sre: also collecting these server-side artifacts helps:
- support debug bundle created with `support-bundle --req req-0a12b3c4,req-0d34f5e6 --range 2026-03-15T14:02:00Z/2026-03-15T14:05:00Z`
- GPU metrics for the pool (nvidia-smi snapshots + per-GPU utilization CSV)
- runtime logs for the model shard that served those requests (stderr/stdout snippets)

marta_support: customer gave sample payloads and the load script. I asked them to run the support-bundle command but they want us to generate the exact command for them to run (they're air-gapped-ish).

eli_sre: ok paste this to them exactly (they need to substitute the support token):
```bash
# run from a host that can reach the control plane
support-bundle collect \
  --customer acme-corp \
  --req-ids req-0a12b3c4,req-0d34f5e6,req-0f56a7b8 \
  --time-range 2026-03-15T14:00:00Z/2026-03-15T14:10:00Z \
  --include gpu-metrics,kv-cache-stats,har,concurrency-profile \
  --output acme-burst-20260315.tar.gz
# then upload to our secure bucket with pre-signed url we will provide
```

sara_support: I'm sending the presigned URL to the customer now. also asked for the client-side concurrency CSV (timestamped request send times) and their HAR if they have it.

marta_support: they uploaded the bundle and added an extra 50 request ids — total 53. link: https://files.internal/acme/acme-burst-20260315.tar.gz (uploaded to secure bucket).

debug-bot: support-bundle: ingest job started for acme-burst-20260315.tar.gz (job id sb-881122).

eli_sre: great. once bundle ingested we'll run a controlled replay against a staging pool with the same model/version and kv-cache settings. if we can reproduce p95 spike we'll attach the wrk command and a minimized promptset for CI regression test.

jay_prodeng: when you run the replay, please capture per-request latencies with token-level breakdown (generation vs network vs queue). that helped last time.

marta_support: noted. i'll coordinate with ACME and post the replay results here. thanks everyone :thumbsup:

sara_support: one last ask — can you confirm billing tier? they said "dedicated-standard" but we need the exact capacity commit so we know pool sizing.

marta_support: confirmed: dedicated-standard, 8xA100 equivalent reserved. added to bundle metadata.

eli_sre: perfect. moving to followup: I'll post results and a minimized repro promptset in ~2 hours after replay.

marta_support: thanks — marking this thread for escalation follow-up.
